arxiv-1811-01489.title: Interference of Electromagnetic waves in the background of the gravitational waves
arxiv-1811-01489.creator: Wenyu Wang, Yang Xu
arxiv-1811-01489.description: Abstract Based on the relationship between proper distance and coordinate distance, the geometrical phenomenon caused by the passing gravitational waves can not be observed locally. The electromagnetic wave equations in the background gravitational waves are studied. We find that the expansion and contraction of wave lengths are always synchronous with the objects it measures.

arxiv-2006-02580.title: Self-referenced hologram of a single photon beam
arxiv-2006-02580.creator: Wiktor Szadowiak †, Sanjukta Kundu †, Jerzy Szuniewicz, Radek Lapkiewicz*
arxiv-2006-02580.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Wiktor Szadowiak †, Sanjukta Kundu †, Jerzy Szuniewicz, Radek Lapkiewicz*. Quantitative characterization of the spatial structure of single photons is essential for free-space quantum communication and quantum imaging. We introduce an interferometric technique that enables the complete characterization of a two-dimensional probability amplitude of a single photon. Importantly, in contrast to methods that use a reference photon for the phase measurement, our technique relies on a single photon interfering with itself.

arxiv-2103-05602.title: A Godunov type scheme and error estimates for multidimensional scalar conservation laws with Panov-type discontinuous flux
arxiv-2103-05602.creator: Shyam Sundar Ghoshal, John D. Towers, Ganesh Vaidya
arxiv-2103-05602.description: Abstract This article concerns a scalar multidimensional conservation law where the flux is of Panov type and may contain spatial discontinuities. We define a notion of entropy solution and prove that entropy solutions are unique. We propose a Godunov-type finite volume scheme and prove that the Godunov approximations converge to an entropy solution, thus establishing existence of entropy solutions.

arxiv-2501-15348.title: ReInc : Scaling Training of Dynamic Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2501-15348.creator: Mingyu Guan, Saumia Singhal, Taesoo Kim, Anand Padmanabha Iyer
arxiv-2501-15348.description: Abstract Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) have gained widespread attention due to their applicability in diverse domains such as traffic network prediction, epidemiological forecasting, and social network analysis. In this paper, we present ReInc , a system designed to enable efficient and scalable training of DGNNs on large-scale graphs.

arxiv-2503-10886.title: Taxonomic Reasoning for Rare Arthropods: Combining Dense Image Captioning and RAG for Interpretable Classification
arxiv-2503-10886.creator: Nathaniel Lesperance, Sujeevan Ratnasingham, Graham W. Taylor
arxiv-2503-10886.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nathaniel Lesperance, Sujeevan Ratnasingham, Graham W. Taylor. In the context of pressing climate change challenges and the significant biodiversity loss among arthropods, automated taxonomic classification from organismal images is a subject of intense research. arxiv-2509-16802.title: Discrepancy And Fair Division For Non-Additive Valuations
arxiv-2509-16802.creator: Max Dupre la Tour, Kaito Fujii
arxiv-2509-16802.description: Abstract We extend the notion of combinatorial discrepancy to non-additive functions. Our main result is an upper bound of O ⁡ ( n ​ log ⁡ ( n ​ k ) ) O(\sqrt{n\log(nk)}) on the non-additive k k -color discrepancy when k k is a prime power. We demonstrate two applications of this result to problems in fair division.

arxiv-2512-09925.creator: Patrick Noras, Jun Myeong Choi, Didier Stricker, Pieter Peers, Roni Sengupta
arxiv-2512-09925.description: Abstract Recent advances in Gaussian Splatting-based inverse rendering extend Gaussian primitives with shading parameters and physically grounded light transport, enabling high-quality material recovery from dense multi-view captures. However, these methods degrade sharply under sparse-view settings, where limited observations lead to severe ambiguity between geometry, reflectance, and lighting.

pmc-13266556.title: High night-to-night variability in obstructive sleep apnea severity is associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease

pmc-13681968.creator: Karuna Sutthibenjakul, Nitchamon Leelarujijaroen, Pannawit Benjhawaleemas, Mantana Saetang
pmc-13681968.description: BackgroundFrailty is common among older adults and is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. Hip fractures are increasingly prevalent in aging populations and frequently require urgent surgical intervention. Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is a common perioperative complication associated with serious postoperative morbidity. However, the relationship between frailty and IOH remains unclear.

pmc-13686543.description: Image quantification is central to modern biomedical research.
